lana_sales: Quick sync — AcmeHealth POC ready to test Private deployment. They want minimal blast radius: prefer PrivateLink but asked about peering. Also need a short-lived hosted API key as backup. Need a checklist and who owns the network handoff.
anya_se: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is our recommended default for cross-account POCs — private DNS + no route-table changes on our side. Peering is fine if they insist on direct VPC-to-VPC routes, but that adds routing + potential transitive routing complexity.
devin_infra: Confirmed. For PrivateLink we'll give them a service name and they'll create a VPCE interface in their VPC. They must pick subnets with free IPs for ENIs (at least 2 AZs recommended). SG on their side should allow outbound to our ENI CIDR or ports 443/8443 depending on TLS termination.
tori_security: A couple security notes: enable VPC flow logs to their S3/CloudWatch, restrict the endpoint SG to only Redwood's service if possible, and we will provide a scoped KMS key policy if they want us to encrypt logs. Also we can issue a short-lived API key for the hosted API with read-only quota for the POC.
lana_sales: Devin — can you post the exact service name and a sample accept flow? Customer will need to request acceptance from their side for peering if we go that route.
devin_infra: Service name (prod test): `com.redwood.vpce.prod-poc-acme`. Sample AWS CLI to create interface endpoint on their side: ```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
  --vpc-id vpc-0abc12345 \
  --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
  --service-name com.redwood.vpce.prod-poc-acme \
  --subnet-ids subnet-0aa subnet-0bb \
  --security-group-ids sg-0a1b2c3d
``` After they create it we'll accept the connection on our side (no route table changes needed).
lana_sales: Nice. What about DNS? They mentioned they want our private hostname to resolve to the interface endpoint.
anya_se: They should enable the private DNS option on the VPCE. If they can't, we can give them the endpoint IPs to add to a private hosted zone A records. Example Terraform snippet for private hosted zone: ```hcl
resource "aws_route53_zone" "acme_private" {
  name = "svc.redwood.internal"
  vpc { vpc_id = "vpc-0abc12345" }
}
resource "aws_route53_record" "redwood_endpoint" {
  zone_id = aws_route53_zone.acme_private.zone_id
  name    = "inference.svc.redwood.internal"
  type    = "A"
  ttl     = 60
  records = ["10.10.5.12", "10.10.7.14"]
}
``` 
devin_infra: For VPC peering option — they'd create a peering connection: ```bash
aws ec2 create-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-id vpc-0abc12345 --peer-vpc-id vpc-0ffedcba --peer-owner-id 123456789012
aws ec2 accept-vpc-peering-connection --vpc-peering-connection-id pcx-0a1b2c3d
``` Then add route table entries in each VPC's route tables for the peer CIDR. Note: peering doesn't work with overlapping CIDRs; check their CIDR plan.
lana_sales: Any NAT/GW considerations? Customer's infra team asked if peering still needs a NAT for outbound internet egress.
devin_infra: Peering doesn't need NAT for internal traffic. But if their subnets are private and need internet egress (e.g., curl to public endpoints), they'll still need a NAT/GW or egress proxy. For PrivateLink traffic to us, no NAT required.
tori_security: Also flag TLS mutual auth if they request it — we can support mTLS at the service boundary, but that needs cert exchange and a CA pinning step. If they'd prefer simpler flow for POC, use standard TLS with IP+SG restrictions.
lana_sales: infra-bot can you create the tracker for the network handoff and include checklist items? I'll send the contact to Acme's cloud eng once we have the service name and temp API key. :pray:
infra-bot: Created ENG-POC-4321: "ACME POC PrivateLink setup" with tasks: provide service name, issue scoped hosted API key (ttl 72h), confirm SG rules, provide endpoint IPs if private DNS not available, create runbook for acceptance.
anya_se: Action items for us: 1) Devin - confirm ENI IP ranges and finalize SG rules. 2) Tori - draft short-term API key policy & KMS notes. 3) Lana - intro to Acme infra with ENG-POC-4321 link. I'll be on the call for the handshake.
lana_sales: Good — I'll aim to schedule the network handoff tomorrow 10:30am PT. If anyone can't make it, post availability here. :calendar:
